items.title: Pink Floyd Announce Animals 50th Anniversary Box Set With Previously Unreleased Tracks
items.summary:
Pink Floyd have scheduled a 50th-anniversary reissue of Animals, the 1977 album that followed Wish You Were Here and preceded The Wall. The set, titled Animals 50, arrives January 22 through Sony Music in multiple formats, with the largest edition running five discs.

That package collects the original album, the 2018 remix, a group of five rarities and a two-disc recording of the band's May 5, 1977 concert at the Oakland Coliseum Arena. The live tapes came from bootlegger Reinhard Hohlwein, who was 19 when he recorded the show. Among the rarities is a previously unreleased Roger Waters song, "Young Nicholas Jon."

Stereogum reported that the first track shared from the box is a radio edit that trims a 10-minute song down to roughly four and a half minutes, a version never commercially released until now. The deluxe edition also includes a 64-page book with a new essay from novelist and Floyd fan Jonathan Lethem, an interview with Hohlwein, and an excerpt from Hipgnosis designer Audrey "Po" Powell's memoir covering the creation of the album's floating-pig cover.

Animals was written almost entirely by Waters, a concept record about the grimness of late-1970s Britain that drew on George Orwell's Animal Farm and the arrival of punk. Built from four long songs bookended by a short intro and outro, it never matched the commercial scale of the albums on either side of it, though it still went quadruple platinum.

The reissue follows last year's 50th-anniversary edition of Wish You Were Here, part of a steady run of archival releases tied to the band's extraordinarily productive stretch in the 1970s. Pre-orders for the box set are open now.

items.title: Lady Gaga, Jack White, Boy George Lead Songwriters Hall of Fame 2027 Nominees
items.summary:
The Songwriters Hall of Fame has published its slate of nominees for the 2027 class, a list that stretches across six decades of popular music. Lady Gaga, Jack White, Boy George, Sia, Vince Gill, Shakira, P!nk, Ne-Yo, will.i.am and Grandmaster Melle Mel are among the performing songwriters up for induction.

Debbie Harry and Chris Stein of Blondie are nominated together, as are Gerry Beckley and Dewey Bunnell of America, the surviving and late members of WAR, and ZZ Top's Billy Gibbons alongside the late Frank Beard and Dusty Hill. The non-performing category leans heavily on hitmaking teams: disco architect Pete Bellotte, Norwegian duo Stargate, Swedish pop writer Andreas Carlsson, British production trio Stock Aitken Waterman, and the 1960s team of Bob Feldman, Jerry Goldstein and Richard Gottehrer.

Also nominated are Kandi Burruss, Boy Meets Girl's George Merrill and Shannon Rubicam, country writers Tom Douglas and Bob McDill, New Edition architect Maurice Starr, Dan Wilson and Toni Wine. The organization lists representative songs for each nominee, ranging from "My Boyfriend's Back" and "A Groovy Kind of Love" to "No Scrubs," "Seven Nation Army" and "Die With a Smile."

Variety reported that songwriters become eligible 20 years after the first commercial release of one of their songs. Voting members have until midnight Eastern on December 14, 2026 to submit ballots, choosing up to three nominees in each of the songwriter and performing songwriter categories.

The ballot's structure means several nominees appear in more than one place: Stargate and Ne-Yo share credits on "Irreplaceable," "So Sick" and "Take a Bow," while Sia's listed songs include "Diamonds," another Stargate co-write. Inductees will be announced after the voting window closes.

items.title: Rush Plan Sphere Residency Celebrating ‘2112’ and ‘Moving Pictures’
items.summary:
Rush will play a five-night residency at the Sphere in Las Vegas next spring, booking May 21, 23, 26, 28 and 30 under the banner Elevate From the Norm. The run follows the band's Fifty Something reunion tour, their first road work since reconvening with drummer Anika Nilles in place of the late Neil Peart.

Each night's set will include complete performances of 2112 and Moving Pictures, the two albums that bracket the band's commercial peak, alongside other hits and deep cuts. Tickets go on sale to the general public Friday, November 13, with presales also beginning Friday and full details posted on the band's website.

Geddy Lee said in a statement that the venue struck him as a natural fit before Rush had any plans to return. "When I first heard of Sphere, I thought to myself, 'Wow, what a shame that Rush is no longer touring, because this venue sounds tailor-made for the kind of visual attitude with which we have always designed our shows,'" he said, adding that the band is "presently working hard to expand our touring concepts and concoct some new madness to suit this incredible venue."

Rolling Stone noted that the Sphere has become the default home for large-scale concert spectacle since U2 opened the building, with Metallica, Eagles, Phish, Dead & Company, Kenny Chesney, the Zac Brown Band, No Doubt and the Backstreet Boys all taking residencies there.

Rush opened the reunion tour with four shows in Los Angeles. Describing the first night to Rolling Stone, Lee said the band settled in quickly: "I was really proud of us that night because we did one of the best versions of that set that we've done yet."
